method: BASELINE. Written straight from the deposited text with the writing-l4-rules skill (and references/regulative.md), from the seat of the individual to whom the Rules are applied, with the design defaults ruled on 2026-10-18 and the rulings on negatives of 2026-11-04 and 2026-11-05 (JUST FALSE where the text says no, NOTHING where it does not answer); date arithmetic in one module, the rules in another, the claimant's questions in a seat module importing them; one regulative rule (rr 547, 550) run by EVALTRACE inside an exported question that takes only plain dates; no REFUSE; checked with the stable l4 of VS Code extension 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset. No pipeline, no coverage table, no independent test pass, no human gate.
edition_encoded: Uniform Civil Procedure Rules 1999 (Qld), SL 1999 No. 111, the version in force from 2026-10-29 (current on 2026-11-06), as deposited at ../../registers/source-bundle/sl-1999-0111.txt (text sha256 683957672f9cf1be3b16ee2b75944d9efd39554a45eb65408def91cbb491c0db per the meta file), converted from the Queensland Legislation HTML view; not the authorised version

seat: the claimant: the individual who brings a claim in the Supreme Court, the District Court or a Magistrates Court of Queensland (usually the plaintiff who is injured or owed money), and the same person where the Rules give them a step to answer (a reply, an answer to a counterclaim) (ucpr-seat.l4)

checks.l4: stable l4 of VS Code extension legalese.l4-vscode 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset
checks.command: l4 run ucpr-dates.l4 ; l4 run ucpr-rules.l4 ; l4 run ucpr-seat.l4 ; l4 run ucpr-cases.l4
checks.result: 116 assertions written, 116 satisfied, 1 #TRACE FULFILLED, 0 errors, 0 warnings in every file (2026-11-07)
checks.note: l4 run exits 0 even when an assertion fails, so the diagnostics were read. Expected values worked by hand from the text.

scope: In: rr 24, 98(1), 137, 138, 164(1)-(2), 169, 189(2)-(3), 214(2)(a), (d), (e) and (3), 281(1), 282-288 with 694 and the fixed items of Schedules 1 and 2, 303(1), 304(1)-(3), 307, 309(1), 355, 358(1)-(3), 359(2), 360, 361, 361A, 362, 389, 514, Schedule 3 'minor claim', 545-547(2), 550(2), 557, 558(1), (2), (4), 681, 691(3)-(4) with Schedule 2's columns, 697, 748. Out: the machinery (Chapter 1 but r 7), service, r 289 (costs-only default judgment) and r 549 (accuracy and supplements of the statement of loss and damage), the content of pleadings and statements, summary judgment, ADR, evidence, trials, special proceedings, probate, security for costs, costs assessment, enforcement, corporations, transitional rules. Reasons in NOTES.md.
